task: Rotate the service account secret for ci-runner after a leaked credential alert. Candidate pool from a 175-entry store across security, CI, and infra projects.

candidate_memories.content: SIEM alert fired at 08:42 UTC: ci-runner service account secret detected in a public GitHub commit; secret must be rotated immediately.
ci-runner secret rotation: generate new secret via vault write auth/approle/role/ci-runner/secret-id, update CIRUNNER_SECRET in vault:/secret/ci/runner, and restart all runner pods.
After rotating, revoke the leaked secret ID in vault using vault write -f auth/approle/role/ci-runner/secret-id-accessor/destroy accessor=<old-accessor>.
Any confirmed credential leak requires an audit of all actions taken using the leaked credential before the rotation is declared complete.
GitHub has been notified via the secret scanning alert; they will auto-revoke the exposed token on their end within 1 h.
deploy-bot service account is separate from ci-runner; it uses a different AppRole and is not affected.
Secret rotation policy requires rotation within 4 h of confirmed leak for CI/CD service accounts.
Old rotation runbook used manual vault CLI commands without the destroy step; updated runbook requires the destroy step.
candidate_memories.notes: stale: old runbook missing destroy step, superseded by current p2

candidate_memories.content: Security team has blocked the leaked credential at the API gateway level as an interim measure.
CI pipeline uses GitHub Actions runners in addition to self-hosted runners; GitHub Actions use OIDC, not the AppRole secret.
Incident severity is P1; incident commander is online in #incident-security.
Secrets must never be committed to version control; pre-commit hook gitleaks is mandatory for all repos.
